sources.text: Will Grand Theft Auto 6 take home Game of the Year? After months of anticipation and constant speculation , we finally know what games will duke it out for the top prize at The Game Awards 2026 . Organizers for the biggest night in gaming announced this year's nominees for Game of the Year , and all the other categories, during a livestream on Tuesday, Nov. 17. Two of the most interesting games to watch out for during this year's awards are Grand Theft Auto 6 and Big Walk . Rockstar's latest blockbuster has been on everyone's mind for years and is finally set to release on Nov. 19. Despite nominations coming out prior to release, GTA 6 is eligible for the Game Awards and is immediately one of the biggest contenders for Game of the Year. Big Walk entered awards season with widespread critical acclaim, but a recent AI-related controversy could spell trouble if members of the voting body object to the use of the technology. Beyond Game of the Year, there are plenty of other categories to get excited about, such as Best Art Direction and Best Performance. With the official nominations announced, the voting body will select winners, who will be revealed during the live show. The 2026 Game Awards will be held on Thursday, Dec. 10 at 4:30 p.m. PT / 7:30 p.m. ET, and there are more ways than ever to tune in . Here are The Game Awards 2026 nominees; we'll update this list as the announcement livestream continues.

sources.text: The actress behind Lucia Caminos, one of the two protagonists at the centre of Grand Theft Auto 6 , has been revealed. With the game’s worldwide launch now just around the corner, we’ve finally got confirmation of one of the two performers. Manni L. Perez takes on the role of Lucia, with her identity being confirmed during The 2026 Game Awards Nominees. She’d long been suspected to be taking on the role, but that rumor has now officially been put to rest just one day ahead of release. If you haven’t already, don’t forget: you can buy Grand Theft Auto 6 here . Thanks to The Game Awards 2026, we now know for certain that Manni L. Perez brings Lucia Caminos to life. Manni L. Perez had long been rumored for the role, and at one point, she even hosted a livestream where viewers repeatedly asked about her connection to GTA 6, but she refused to acknowledge either the game or her character ; we can only imagine how strict Rockstar’s NDAs have been. Still, it’s great to finally put a name to one of the two characters who are already incredibly recognisable, though we’re still waiting on an official reveal for her partner in crime, Jason Duval. The pair will undoubtedly become two of the most iconic protagonists in the franchise, with Rockstar confident that Lucia can “stand tall” with the likes of Niko Bellic and Arthur Morgan. Many were hoping for an official reveal by Rockstar, especially with the game just a day away now. However, Manni L. Perez’s nomination for Best Performance seems to have beaten Rockstar to the punch. A complete voice cast list is yet to be revealed, but with GTA 6 now just a day away, we shouldn’t have to wait much longer to discover everyone involved. The in-game credits will eventually provide those answers, although you’ll have to put in a fair amount of time before reaching them, particularly if you’re hoping to earn that elusive Platinum trophy. sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 and Nintendo lead The Game Awards 2026 nominations Grand Theft Auto 6 has received multiple nominations at The Game Awards 2026, providing an early indication of the critical response to Rockstar’s long-awaited release. Producer and host Geoff Keighley announced The Game Awards 2026 nominations during a live stream on Tuesday, which, as usual, were chosen by a voting jury of media publications, including this website, VGC. More than 30 awards are up for grabs this year (see the full list of nominees below), and the winners will again be determined by a blended vote between the voting jury (90%) and public voting (10%). In total, Grand Theft Auto 6 is up for 8 awards, including Game of the Year, Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Art Direction, Best Score, Best Audio Design, and Best Performance for Manni L. Perez as Lucia . The other most nominated games are Control Resonant (8) and Resident Evil Requiem (8), Phantom Blade Zero (5), Big Walk (4), 007 First Light (4), and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (4). Nintendo is the most nominated publisher with 12 nominations, followed by Capcom (11), Annapurna (9) and PlayStation (9), and Rockstar Games (8) and Xbox (8). The six nominees for Game of the Year include Grand Theft Auto 6, 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Outro representante da LOUD é Erde, indicado individualmente ao prêmio de Melhor Atleta de Esports. A presença dos brasileiros reforça a participação do país em diferentes áreas da indústria, desde a criação de conteúdo até as competições profissionais. sources.title: GTA 6 Officially Becomes Clear Game Awards 2026 Frontrunner
sources.text: Almost no one has played it yet, but GTA 6 has eight nominations The Game Awards revealed its full list of nominees today , and things went as many expected : Grand Theft Auto 6 is the clear frontrunner in the 2026 Game of the Year race. GTA 6 scored an impressive eight nominations, including Best Narrative, Best Action/Adventure Game, Best Game Direction, and Game of the Year. Control: Resonant is tied for second with six nominations, earning nods for Game of the Year, Best Narrative, and Best Game Direction. Resident Evil Requiem also has six nominations, including for Game of the Year . GTA 6's dominance puts it in an unusual situation . The game is up for awards, but the vast majority of players haven't gotten their hands on it yet. These nominations are obviously a sign that critics who received early codes are very high on the game, but we have little idea why . That said, the specific nomination categories offer some insights. It was nominated for Best Action Adventure Game, implying critics liked its gameplay, as well as Best Narrative, suggesting its storytelling landed for many. We won’t have to wait long for full explanations about why GTA 6 is such a hit with The Game Awards' judges — GTA 6 is releasing on Nov. 19 — but it’s still an awkward situation that will invite plenty of questions. Did the voters get enough time to finish the game? Did every judge have an opportunity to play, or only a few? Would people have voted differently if they had gotten a chance to see the broader cultural reaction to the game? It's a strange scenario. Beyond the frontrunner GTA 6 , there are a few other games with a reasonable chance at winning Game of the Year. Control: Resonant exceeded expectations, racking up an impressive number of nominations beyond its GOTY nod, including Best Game Direction. While it didn't score quite as highly with critics overall compared to many other Remedy games, it clearly landed with the judges. The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time has a shot, as it's currently the highest-rated game released this year on both Metacritic and OpenCritic. Reviewers praised it as an outstanding remake that maintains what made the original a classic while adding slick improvements throughout . Still, because it's a remake rather than an all-new experience, it's probably less likely to win big. It also doesn't help that it has fewer nominations than several other Game of the Year contenders. As a great entry in a beloved series that's tied for the second most nominations, Resident Evil: Requiem also has a decent chance. That said, the significant fall-off in its second half, which is likely what prevented it from cracking a 90 on review aggregator sites, may be a significant liability. Phantom Blade 0 also arguably overperformed in nominations with five. It received very positive reviews for its sense of visual style and for breaking away from the soulslike formula. Lastly, there's 007: First Light . It was praised for its stellar introduction and story, but tied for the fewest nominations among the Game of the Year candidates, with four total. Of course, there were some snubs as well. Despite very positive reviews, Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave only received a single nomination and was omitted from the Best Narrative, Best Soundtrack, and Game of the Year categories. While some thought that Big Walk may be able to earn a Game of the Year nomination, it was restricted to the indie categories. All things considered, this year brought us many great games, but few outstanding ones with wide appeal. It looks like Game of the Year is very much Grand Theft Auto 6 ’s race to lose.

sources.text: Next Xbox console is "designed to be the ultimate gaming machine" by removing the "arbitrary constraints between console and PC games" Xbox VP of Next Generation Jason Ronald has clarified that Project Helix is "designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games, not a PC that can also play console games." sources.title: The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" says Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time
sources.text: "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering." Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC". The company has also underlined the importance of using gen-AI-adjacent "neural rendering" technology going forwards, and a desire to remove "all the barriers of play that have historically existed" - notably in making the past generations of games playable. The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday , and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald said, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games. "We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added. "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it." Notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation. "It's about deeper immersion," Ronald said. "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering." While referencing the global component shortage and exorbitant prices of computer hardware, he added: "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years." Xbox boss Asha Sharma also recently talked up the importance of generative-AI-sounding technology in Xbox's future , saying "too many ideas never become games", and that "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations". Another key part of Xbox's Helix vision is compatibility and game preservation. "Game preservation is core to Xbox," Ronald went as far as to say. "Not only do we feel like it's the right thing for the industry, we feel a deep responsibility as one of its biggest platforms and publishers. For the first 30 years of game development, nobody really thought about game preservation when they were designing their hardware, when they were building their games." Xbox is apparently working with game-makers to ensure games can not only be played now but also 20 to 30 years into the future. The other key facet of Microsoft's push the familiar Play Anywhere mantra, whereby one game can be played across multiple devices, maintaining your game-progress as you go. This is fundamental to Microsoft's handheld-and-console Helix plan, and something we've seen the company dry-run with the Xbox ROG Ally X handheld . "It's this notion that not only does my library move with me, but my progress moves with me as well," Ronald said. "Because I fully expect that when I'm in the middle of an 80-hour RPG, if I'm 25 hours into that and I want to play it on another device, I should be able to instantly resume from where I was. Those are things that today are becoming more common, but I think in the future it's going to be a baseline expectation of all players." Ronald wouldn't be drawn on the issue of price regarding Project Helix - a recent report suggested Helix could be priced up to $1800 - referring to it only as both "a challenging time" but an "exciting one", because "we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable". Ronald also wouldn't reference a release date, though the report referenced above suggested the handheld Helix machine will release next holiday, 2027, and the console Helix machine the year after. The next generation, then, seems to be around the corner.

sources.title: Xbox afirma que Project Helix é um console capaz de rodar jogos de PC — e não o contrário
sources.text: A Microsoft divulgou novos detalhes sobre o Project Helix, seu console de nova geração, e reforçou a ideia de que o videogame é capaz de rodar jogos de PC — mas não um PC que consegue rodar jogos de console. Em entrevista publicada na revista especial de 25 anos do Xbox, Jason Ronald, vice-presidente da próxima geração da marca, explicou que o projeto foi desenvolvido para funcionar como um console tradicional, e não como um computador com recursos de videogame. “O Helix foi projetado para ser um console capaz também de rodar jogos do seu PC. Não é um PC que também roda jogos de console”, afirmou Ronald. O executivo também destacou que o aparelho pretende eliminar barreiras entre as bibliotecas de jogos de PC e Xbox, na intenção de manter a experiência simples e intuitiva para os jogadores. Segundo Ronald, a proposta do Project Helix é reunir diferentes bibliotecas em um único dispositivo e permitir com que os jogadores acessem seus títulos com mais facilidade. O console também deve oferecer compatibilidade com quatro gerações de jogos e preservar o progresso das contas Xbox. O executivo explicou que a experiência poderá ser adaptada a diferentes perfis de jogadores. Quem preferir uma experiência tradicional terá acesso rápido aos jogos, enquanto usuários mais avançados poderão personalizar configurações e opções de desempenho. “Quando penso no que torna um console mágico, é o fato de ele tornar meus jogos instantaneamente acessíveis e prontos para jogar”, afirmou Ronald. Ele também destacou que os jogadores não precisarão se preocupar com atualizações de drivers ou configurações típicas de um PC. A ideia, segundo o executivo, é criar uma plataforma que reúna a praticidade dos consoles com a flexibilidade dos computadores. “Quando pensamos no Project Helix, ele foi realmente concebido para ser a máquina de jogos definitiva — uma que remove todas as barreiras de jogo que existiram historicamente”, declarou. Durante a entrevista, Ronald também comentou sobre os desafios de desenvolver um novo console em meio à crise de componentes de PC. Segundo ele, a Microsoft está investindo em tecnologias como a renderização neural para melhorar o desempenho sem exigir mais poder computacional ou memória. “É definitivamente um momento desafiador, mas, como designer de sistemas e plataformas, também é um dos momentos mais empolgantes”, afirmou. O executivo explicou que a equipe busca novas soluções para avançar tecnologicamente e, ao mesmo tempo, manter os custos de produção e os preços sustentáveis. Ronald citou a renderização neural como uma das principais apostas para a próxima geração. A tecnologia pode abranger diferentes técnicas de processamento de imagem, como aprimoramento de resolução, geração de quadros e reconstrução de iluminação, embora a Microsoft ainda não tenha detalhado como pretende aplicá-la no Project Helix. O executivo também afirmou que a próxima geração não deve ser definida apenas por especificações tradicionais — como resolução 8K ou taxas de atualização de 240 Hz. Para ele, o foco estará em novas experiências de jogo, maior imersão e avanços visuais mais eficientes. E você, está ansioso para conhecer a próxima geração de consoles? sources.title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is GTA 5 without the finesse - so why is the 2004 classic such a strange delight to return to?
sources.text: There is a place in Whitewood Estates where a promising stretch of blacktop suddenly gives way to the desert. It feels like the road has been erased, a sentence left unfinished. It's quietly strange, a weird bit of urban wrongfooting. But I guess it makes some kind of sense. California, after all, is home to California City, a town that was planned and then never really built. It sits out there now, north of Los Angeles, streets laid out but slowly being eaten by the sand and dirt. Still, 14,000 people lived there as of 2018. Design limitation or something stranger, this digital dead end is a reminder that all of this land, so modern, so ancient - all of this is spook country. It's fitting I guess that GTA San Andreas is such a strange delight to return to. As I've waited, like everyone else, for GTA 6 , I've been back here in the GTA games of the past, via the slightly dodgy remasters from a few years ago. And what's come through for me, spending a few idle mornings messing around in San Andreas, a game I thought I knew pretty well, is how beautifully odd everything is now. The best part of 20 years have given a game that once strained against its host technology a genuine aesthetic. Surprisingly sparse in detailing, as angular and sheer as dream architecture, in love with expanses, San Andreas is perfectly placed, it seems to me, to capture just how weird California can be. California and Nevada. This is the part I always forget. I mainly think of San Andreas these days through the lens of GTA 5 , which gives you LA and its surroundings but lets the single city serve as the star. It has a bigger footprint than the earlier game, sure, but it uses that space to go deep on the detailing and the sense of a singular, fiercely specific place. San Andreas meanwhile offers three cities - and one of them isn't actually in California. Alongside spins on LA and San Francisco, you get a version of Las Vegas. It's quite neat really: the three points of some arcane spiritual triangle. The kind of thing Marvel Whiteside Parsons, aerospace engineer and Actual Wizard, might have scratched in the dust of his backyard to help him control the weather. He lived - and died - in Pasadena, so all this would have been familiar anyway. There is a classic moment in every GTA. A moment where the map opens up in the early games, or when you explore enough in the later games, and simply get to understand the audacity of what is being attempted here. In San Andreas, and this feels apt, the best way to have this moment is to break the rules, sneaking into the open map before the game is fully ready for you. An early mission allows you to step away from the critical path, as it were, and peg it to the airport in Los Santos, where a plane is waiting to be pinched. Taxi, feel the thrust, and you're off. LA beneath you - sorry, Los Santos - and on the horizon a dinkytown version of the Golden Gate Bridge and the MGM Grand. Dinkytown is the word. From the sky, the huge map of San Andreas, which still feels like an incredible piece of work - such ambition! - can look like toys laid out on a duvet in the remasters. Coming back from GTA 5, a masterpiece of texture, the cities of San Andreas in particular feel very weird - cramped and condensed and wonderfully stagey, arranged the way a kid might jury-rig them together from shoeboxes and stray cardboard. On your way out of Grove Street early on you pass the Los Santos equivalent of the Hollywood sign, looming so close the way it does in the movies but not in the actual city and you feel you could touch it. Downtown is reduced to a handful of the best buildings - it's always pleasing to see the one from the brilliant first act of Speed made the cut - but still manages to capture the important stuff too, which in this case is the way that modern LA looms somewhat cruelly over the old city, captured with a strange sepulchral dignity in the form of the City Hall, so easy to spot but now so small! Elsewhere, the ersatz Las Vega Strip looks like a drawing based on memory - a few of the classic shapes are there, but it's a sketch of a place. In this way, I guess, it captures a truth about Las Vegas. Also, perhaps, it's an admission that this is a town comfortably out of the reach of satire. As for San Francisco, it's a 60s cop movie delight to fishtail around. It nails the hills and what more do you need for a game with cars in it? Taken as a whole these cities feel mesmerising now. And it's the limitations that make them sing, I think: those sheer granite canyons of downtown LA with its towering blocks of architecture and surprisingly thin traffic, with only the very faintest of ambient soundtracks that ensures any gunfire will pop and clap and shake you out of your seat. (Remember, I am playing the remasters and sound effects may be missing.) This is the LA of Repo Man rather than Heat - an otherland where the buildings feel alien, even the air feels alien. At night, palm trees stand out against a sky that glows a deep, clean red. GTA 5 would finesse all of this, the skyboxes and whatnot, but perhaps in that finessing something is lost. (Both games, incidentally, have such a talent for capturing California's kitsch excess that they perhaps miss some of the sweeter truths, such as the astonishing diversity of cultures a city like Los Angeles finds homes for. But how could any game do that justice?) GTA 6 isn't out until later this week and it's now up for Game of the Year alongside seven other awards at the Keighleys, which is set to air on Thursday December 10, 2026. We don't even have reviews for Rockstar's latest yet, but I guess that's a good sign that it'll be pretty good when it arrives later this week. The nominees for The Game Awards Game of the Year are GTA 6, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , Resident Evil Requiem, 007 First Light, Phantom Blade Zero, and Control Resonant. Meanwhile, other potential Game of the Year candidates like Pragmata, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave and Pokemon: Pokopia have been represented in the genre categories. As for the penultimate award for Best Game Direction, unsurprisingly Rockstar and Capcom are in the category with GTA 6 and Resident Evil Requiem respectively. But Capcom pulled out another nomination in this category with Pragmata, Remedy for Control Resonant, and S-Game for Phantom Blade Zero also in the running. While games like God of War Ragnarok and Dragon Age Inquisition were released pretty close to the cutoff date, this marks the first time that a game that hasn't released yet has been nominated for Game of the Year at The Game Awards. And if GTA 6 wins, it will mark Rockstar's first Game of the Year win at the show after God of War beat Red Dead Redemption 2 at the 2018 show. sources.title: Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic director was "circling" a revival of BioWare's KOTOR for years
sources.text: "What if we put a dent in the universe and made, essentially, the next in the line of Knights of the Old Republic games?" I imagine most BioWare fans would argue that the studio's peak happened somewhere between Dragon Age: Origins and Mass Effect 2. For me, though, the absolute high point was Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and I was always a little bitter that the devs moved on to create Mass Effect rather than finishing Revan's story in a proper KOTOR 3. That's why seeing Casey Hudson, original director of KOTOR, return with a spiritual successor in Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic is so exciting, and it's apparently been a long time coming. "It is really a dream project for us," Hudson says in an interview with The Fourth Curtain podcast . After leaving BioWare – for a second time – in 2020, he founded a new studio called Humanoid Origin, which was developing a "sci-fi action RPG" that would've been a "brand-new IP." That studio shuttered in 2024 after an "unexpected shortfall of funding," leaving Hudson to figure out what to do next. "We had lots of ideas, including, like, 'Do we get funding to continue with what we were doing? Are there other paths forward?' But over the years – myself and folks from our team, we worked on the original Knights of the Old Republic way back in the day, and since then BioWare also had the Old Republic MMO. So we've kept up connections with folks at Lucasfilm ," he says. Some time after Humanoid Origin shut down, Hudson explains, "the head of Disney Games reached out and said, 'Hey, what if we put a dent in the universe and made, essentially, the next in the line of Knights of the Old Republic games? The spiritual successor.'" Hudson says he'd been "circling" the idea of returning to KOTOR for some time. "It's something that I would love to do, but I was either doing other things or other projects. There were times when maybe it wasn't right for Lucasfilm, or they weren't ready for it. There wasn't really a fit." He was excited both by the possibility of returning to KOTOR and bringing back "some of the the top folks we've worked with," but surviving a studio shutdown leads you to "become the most skeptical person on earth," he says. "You don't really trust anyone to follow through with a deal or funding until things are signed, done, and legit." Getting those contracts finalized is how Hudson spent "the first half" of 2025. Then he spent the rest of the year "just starting to assemble our team, doing a prototype, and then creating the announcement trailer." Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Yes, that means that Fate of the Old Republic had only barely entered development at the time of its reveal at The Game Awards last year, but Hudson seems confident we won't be waiting forever for it to be finished. The team works "at a very brisk pace," and he says we should expect "new announcements" sometime next year. Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic could be going for "a more simple hero's journey" to avoid BioWare's "self-indulgent" storytelling, says ex-Dragon Age boss Dustin Bailey joined the GamesRadar team as a Staff Writer in May 2022, and is currently based in Missouri. He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator. sources.text: Includes the return of Now & Later Packs, MLB The Show 26 community stats, and more. Before we dive into new information on MLB The Show 27, let’s take a look back. As we reflect on 2026, two things stand out above everything else: the incredible passion and support of the MLB The Show community, and our need to better communicate and react to community feedback going forward. Whether you’ve been playing for decades or joined us for the first time this year, you’ve helped make this another special chapter in our franchise’s history. While we’re proud of what our team accomplished this year, we recognize that the heart of MLB The Show has always been its community. Since launch, you’ve hit an astonishing: You’ve also drawn 123,300,616 walks and racked up a staggering 2,130,551,161 strikeouts. It seems we have some work to do on our collective plate discipline and pitch recognition! But it’s not all strikeouts. You’ve also recorded 18,666,758 Perfect-Perfect hits and scored an incredible 2,506,757,548 runs. And if those numbers weren’t impressive enough, the community collectively spent the equivalent of 31,541 years playing MLB The Show this year. This year was not without some issues and hopefully over the next few months we’ll show you how we’ve made improvements in a host of areas.Your stories, feedback, creativity, and passion remind us why we do what we do. We don’t take your time, trust, or support for granted, and we’re incredibly fortunate to have a community that cares so deeply about the game. From all of us at San Diego Studio, thank you for another unforgettable year. We’re excited about what lies ahead and look forward to continuing this journey together. So, what lies ahead? We’re eager to share the exciting new features and improvements coming to MLB The Show 27, but it’s still a little too early to reveal what’s in store. However, there’s one announcement we can’t wait to make: The Tech Test is officially returning for MLB The Show 27. Tech Tests are invaluable to the development process. They help our team identify bugs, evaluate performance, and gather meaningful feedback from the community before the game officially launches. Now, you might be wondering: If Tech Tests are so important, why haven’t we held one since MLB The Show 23? That’s a fair question. Game development is challenging, and each year brings its own set of difficult decisions and competing priorities. Some of those decisions resulted in us not holding Tech Tests for the past few years. We appreciate your patience, passion, and continued support, and we’re looking forward to having you be part of the process again. We will provide more details on the Tech Test in the new year. There is still more ahead for MLB The Show 26 , and the time you spend playing can give you a head start in MLB The Show 27. Now & Later packs are coming back. Now & Later Packs contain items you can use now in MLB The Show 26, with the added bonus of allowing you to redeem The Show Packs “later” in MLB The Show 27 at no additional cost. Each Now & Later Pack you earn playing Diamond Dynasty Content in MLB The Show 26 on console will give out a Now & Later voucher that will automatically be redeemed into The Show Packs when logging into MLB The Show 27 on console during its standard release. Make sure you log into ‘27 with the same account you used to earn Now & Later Packs in ‘26. While that’s all for today, in the meantime, get a head start and start earning those Now & Later Packs in MLB The Show 26. We look forward to sharing more soon and are excited about what’s to come in 2027. In the meantime, for the latest MLB The Show news, head to TheShow.com , sign up for The Scouting Report , and follow our official social channels.

stories.title: Sony Defeats $2.6 Billion Class-Action Lawsuit Over Claimed PlayStation Store Monopoly
stories.summary: The UK case has rumbled along for years, but a London court ruled the evidence wasn't there

sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Sony Defeats $2.6 Billion Class-Action Lawsuit Over Claimed PlayStation Store Monopoly
sources.text: Since 2022 , Sony has been facing the British equivalent of a class action lawsuit that could have cost the company as much as $2.6 billion had it lost. It, however, did not. As reported byÂ The Game Business , the lawsuit brought by consumer advocate Alex Neill claimed that Sony was operating a “near monopoly” via the PlayStation Store, and sued the Japanese company on behalf of nine million UK PlayStation owners, but today the claims were rejected, and the case has been dismissed. The reported financial goal of the lawsuit has wildly swung about over the years, cited as $5.9 billion in 2022 , then $7.9 billion by 2023 , and then down to $2.6 billion in May of this year. Whatever the number, the case being made was that by not allowing third-party stores to sell digital PlayStation games, Sony effectively has a monopoly from which it extracts 30 percent of every sale. This, said Neill and the PlayStation You Owe Us campaign, was an “abuse” of Sony’s “dominant position,” forcing customers to pay “too much for digital games and in-game content purchased through the PlayStation Store.” A previous attempt to have the case thrown out was rejected in 2023, and then things looked far worse for Sony when it lost a very similar case in California in May of this year , to the tune of $7.8 billion. And there’s the rather pertinent point that Sony absolutely does dominate sales of digital games on PlayStation, and that’s only going to get a whole lot worse as the megacorp phases out physical media entirely. Yet, following May’s trial , London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal has rejected the argument and ruled that, as reported by TGB , “the claim failed to establish that PlayStation infringed competition law.” The argument against a monopoly was based on the wider competition of Xbox, Nintendo, and PC, alongside the (current) option to buy physical versions of games. Allowing third-party stores onto the PlayStation could, the court said, impact security, which interestingly was the failed argument Google made in its battle against Epic. The tribunal also said Neill had failed to prove that Sony’s profits were “excessive,” likely given that 30 percent cuts are pretty much an industry standard. sources.title: PlayStation beats $2.6 billion lawsuit over its game prices
sources.text: PlayStation will not be compelled to allow third-party stores on its consoles A lawsuit brought against PlayStation over its storefront and game prices has been dismissed. The UK class action lawsuit was brought against PlayStation by Alex Neill,Â representing PlayStation users who complained that they were trapped and forced to use the PS Store. They argued that PlayStation’s 30% cut on all game sales led to games being sold for “excessive and unfair prices”. If PlayStation lost the lawsuit, the plaintiffs were seeking $2.6 billion in damages. As reported by The Game Business , Londonâs Competition Appeal Tribunal has rejected this argument entirely, dismissing the idea that PlayStation has a “near monopoly” on the market. However, part of its argument was that users could instead opt to buy games physically – something which will not remain the case for much longer. PlayStation says it will phase out physical game sales by January 2028 . With that said, PlayStation users might not have much more luck with this argument when physical games are phased out either. That is because the court was not convinced that PlayStation games were priced too highly on the PS Store, or that game prices would be brought down if PlayStation allowed third-party storefronts on its systems.Â PlayStation is facing similar lawsuits in other regions, so it remains to be seen if it can defeat all of them. If any of them were to side against the company, that could set a significant precedent in the gaming industry, opening all platform owners up to third-party storefronts. For the time being, though, the status quo has been maintained with this UK ruling. Right now, the big three console giants – PlayStation, Xbox , and Nintendo – all maintain their own storefronts on their platforms. The only exception to this is Valve , which allows users to buy games from other storefronts on the Steam Machine and Steam Deck. Xbox’s storefront is also available on PC , as is Xbox Game Pass.

sources.title: London court tosses $2.6 billion Sony lawsuit claiming it holds "near monopoly" on PlayStation Store
sources.text: The case was dismissed entirely and unanimously A $2.6 billion lawsuit alleging Sony holds a "near monopoly" through the PlayStation Store, and has used its position to charge more and extract "unfair" margins on sales, has been dismissed by the London Competition Appeal Tribunal. As The Game Business spotted, the class action-style case case was dismissed entirely via unanimous judgment . "The Class Representative has not satisfied us that Sony is dominant in any relevant market for the purposes of assessing any anti-competitive infringement by Sony," the concluding remarks read. The question was not whether Sony is dominant on the PlayStation Store. Of course Sony is king on its own platform. The court essentially examined whether that dominance creates or supports unfair, illegally monopolistic conditions. The court ruled that it does not, and for a variety of factors, including competition provided by physical game sales, as well as platforms like Xbox, Nintendo, and PC. Additionally, it found that letting third-party stores on the PlayStation platform would require "significant adaptation of the platform and its operations" at "significant cost and effort," likely leading to "reduced security in the platform architecture and with potentially reduced performance." The impending end of physical PlayStation games, with Sony looking to phase out discs for new games in January 2028, obviously looms over the discussion here. The court did acknowledge it, but only via post-trial submissions, as this lawsuit stretches back to 2022, far before Sony announced the end of discs. But I do think the court's comments are relevant and interesting in general.
